pll2d1c1-d1e3514.summary: Opens the treatise on creation: Gen 1:1 shows God as creator and beginning of time and of all visible and invisible creatures. Moses, inspired, shows the world made by one principle, against those holding many beginningless principles, such as Plato's God, exemplar, and matter, uncreated, with God as craftsman, not creator. A creator is one who makes something from nothing.
claims: God is the one creator and principle.
Plato's three uncreated principles are rejected.

pl-l2d1c1.summary: Opens Book 2 on creation. Gen 1:1 shows God to be the creator and the beginning of time and of all visible and invisible creatures, one principle, against those who posited several eternal principles, like Plato's God, exemplar, and matter, with God as craftsman rather than creator. A creator makes something from nothing.
claims: God is the creator and the one principle of all things.
There are not several uncreated principles.
Plato's three principles (God, exemplar, matter) are rejected.
To create is to make something from nothing.
